slides.title: Cost of quality

to determine the extent to which its resources are used for activities that
prevent poor quality, that appraise the quality of the organization's products
or services, and that result from internal and external failures.
Having such information allows an organization to determine the potential
savings to be gained by implementing process improvements.
Cost of Good Quality (COGQ) and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ)
COGQ consists of the cost of quality conformance, including any associated costs
with both appraisal and prevention, whereas COPQ involves all the
nonconformance costs that are both internal and external to the company.
